one_line: A human-authority boundary for reviewing and committing agent-proposed shared changes.
what_it_does: Stages typed proposals, lets a reviewer accept/reject each operation, and commits only the accepted subset.
leverage_rationale: Atomic typed proposals against revisions plus human review and selective commit provide reliable shared-state governance beyond UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies get_current_view, propose_changes, and commit_proposal tools.
Canonical scenario visibly separates five proposed changes, four accepted, one rejected, and committed result.

execution_evidence: Frames show shared plan, agent proposal, review decisions, and final accepted subset.
About text describes browser-local two-person roles and revision checks.
impact_rationale: Teams need safe ways to let agents prepare shared work without allowing unilateral changes; the authority boundary directly addresses that need.
impact_evidence: Observer/reviewer permissions and selective commit are concrete collaboration safeguards.
creativity_rationale: The proposal-versus-commit interaction and per-operation review are a clear, original treatment of agent collaboration governance.
creativity_evidence: Visible canonical outcome changes after rejecting one proposed QA compression.
red_flags: Browser-local scope may limit real-world collaboration; production persistence not established.
standouts: Excellent visible authority boundary and selective commit model.
advance_reason: Strong governance-focused WebMCP concept with clear demonstrated state transitions.
